answer: Agents register by completing a sequential delay proof after drawing a random wharf from a shared nebula of docking slots. The proof cannot start until the inlet assignment is revealed, blocking precomputation. An attacker spawning 80 identities must therefore finish 80 separate sequential proofs, each requiring roughly 12 minutes of non-parallelizable compute, for a total of 16 hours of serial work or equivalent dedicated hardware. Honest agents pay the cost only once. If the nebula is too small, collision rates rise and honest agents simply retry.
